name: Dengka
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at the stated place (Edwards 2021 sec 2.4.1 p.35) in a file we hold, and Dengka is explicitly within that section's scope (Table 2.3 row, fn.8, p.35 remark on Dengka recordings). The classification 'fixed penultimate with alternating secondary stress leftward' (stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 (1 = a stressed syllable)) matches the quotation exactly and is corroborated by the two best neighbouring descriptions we hold: Jonker 1915 sec 4 (pan-Rote: accent always on the penult of di- and trisyllabic stems, no shift under pronominal suffixes) and Tamelan 2021 sec 2.2.5 (Dela, Dengka's closest West Rote relative: penultimate vowel of the root, secondary stress on the initial syllable of two-foot roots, clitics/prefixes/paragogic vowels extrametrical, spectrogram given). Nothing found suggests Dengka deviates. The record is 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced' only because the deciding statement is a Rote-wide g

sources.citation: Edwards 2021, Rote-Meto Comparative Dictionary, ANU Press PDF sec 2.4.1 p.
sources.quote: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of a word with secondary stress assigned to every second syllable to the left.
